summary: @or-sdk/settings preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that unconditionally downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases (v1.3.13) into a temporary directory and then invokes it against a bundled sibling file `math_init.js` at the package root. `setup.mjs` is obfuscated in the obfuscator.io style (`_0xNNNNNN` identifiers with per-function string-alias objects that hide the download URL) and `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line Bun single-file bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with a shuffled string-array function and a ~7000-entry mixed constants table plus a decoder — its behavior cannot be inspected from the Node source. The package advertises itself as a Settings SDK (`main: dist/cjs/index.js`, `src/Settings.ts`); nothing in the SDK source or shipped dist references `math_init.js`, so the file's only role is to be executed by the installed Bun binary at install time. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: pull a second language runtime specifically to execute opaque bytes that Node would not normally load, evading scanners that trace only Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
